source.text: Welcome to this Exposure Ninja digital marketing course all about conversion rate optimization. Now, conversion rate optimization is one of my favorite areas of digital marketing for the simple reason that there is no faster way to generate significant improvements in the results that your website brings for you than improving its conversion rate. Here's why CRO, conversion rate optimization, is so important. In almost everywhere else in digital marketing, people are so focused on driving traffic to their website. So whether it's running Facebook ads or Google ads or doing SEO or blogging or social media, YouTube, Facebook, LinkedIn, whatever, everyone always focuses on traffic, i.e. getting more people to their website. But what very few people ever focus on is what happens to that traffic when it hits your website. And that's usually the main area that's letting people down. In fact, many websites out there will have a 0.5 or even lower rate conversion rate. So 0.5% conversion rate means that you get 0.5 leads for every 100 visits. Or in other words, you need to get 200 visitors on your site to get one lead or sale. This conversion rate optimization piece helps you to take that 0.5 and turn it into a number that makes a lot more sense for your business. For example, at Exposure Ninja, we regularly build sites that have a conversion rate of between 2% to 10%, sometimes even higher. So that means that that website might be getting 2 to 10 leads for every 100 visitors instead of half a lead for every 100 visitors. What this does to the numbers across your digital marketing is absolutely transformational. Let's imagine that you're paying1 pound per click through your Google ad campaign and you've got a website that converts at 1% conversion rate. That means you have to spend 100 or 100 clicks for £1 each to get each lead. That gives you a cost per lead of £100. Let's now say that you're able to make some changes to your conversion rate using the processes I'm going to show you today and you can take that 1% and turn it into a 3%. Now you get three leads for every 100 visitors or £100 spent. That takes your cost per lead from £100 to £33. That's a huge huge difference. That means you can afford to spend more on your ads. It means that you can do other advertising that you maybe wouldn't have been able to afford to do at the lower conversion rate. It really is transformational. So, I'm going to show you a whole bunch of stuff in this session. We're going to look at loads of different theoretical stuff first of all to give you some ideas about what your conversion rate optimization processes should be and in particular what the visitor lead sale process is going to be on your website. And then at the end, I'm going to show you some tools that you can be using to implement this stuff on your site. The precise implementation obviously is going to depend on the website platform that you're using, but throughout we're going to be sharing examples of websites that are doing a really good job of this. And then in that final video, I'm going to show you some tools that you can apply whatever your website is to start making a change to your conversion rate optimization. Really hope you enjoy this. Like I say, it's one of my favorite topics. And if you have any questions at all, don't forget you can hit us up, you can email the uh company or you can drop a message in the Facebook group and we'll be happy to help. Enjoy. Okay, so this video is all about conversion rate optimization. We're going to give a quick whistle stops tour of some of the principles that we're going to be going through in the further videos. So this whole course is broken into two sections. uh the first section and it's much larger of the two sections is the theory behind this stuff. And the reason that we're talking a lot about the theory behind this stuff is that really the implementation is fairly simple. It's very quick and easy to put a button on a website or to get a form showing on a website. But unless you know what to write around that form and the psychological principles to use on the rest of the page in order to get someone to fill in that form, the form itself doesn't really mean anything. And that's one of the first lessons of conversion rate optimization. People get caught up thinking that it's all about changing the color of a button or putting a form here and then they're disappointed when their websites don't get the results that they want. And the reason is it's because it's not about just having a form there. It's about having a form that people actually want to fill in in order to become a lead. So, we're going to spend a good amount of time talking about the theory first and then we're going to look at how to implement it because once you know the principles behind it, everything else will make loads more sense. So, the goal for this course is that you have a clear conversion and sales process that starts from your advert and finishes with a client or a sale. Okay, so we're talking about the process from turning someone from being traffic into being a lead or a sale. Now, this is actually part of the Exposure Ninja Star Marketing System. We're going to be looking at the process piece, which is right at the bottom here. And this is all about turning visitors into leads or sales. So many websites are just put up there and then they hope the owner of the website hopes that it's going to turn into business and they're really disappointed when it doesn't. The reason that it doesn't turn into business for them is because that website hasn't been built with these principles in mind. So the qualified customer closer is the process that we're going to be going through today. And there are six different elements within closer. So the first is credibility. This is about how your website demonstrates credibility to your customer. If your customer doesn't believe that what you do is good, they will not convert. And this is one of the most straightforward principles to help people understand because in real life, you know, offline, we know this to be true. We need to believe that someone is good before we're going to consider doing business with them. But on the internet, people make the mistake and think that just because you put a website up that people are therefore just going to somehow magically convert and you don't really need to do anything else with them. Well, I'm going to show you some different examples of how to exhibit credibility on a website and we're going to look at some websites that perform particularly well um because of their use of credibility. In the video after that, we'll go through lure and how to use lure in order to attract people and make them want to become a lead or sale. This is particularly important for lead generation businesses. So, service companies that sell a service rather than e-commerce businesses where the lure is obviously buying the product that you're selling. So, it's pretty straightforward for e-commerce businesses. But for a lot of service companies, they just don't consider this at all. And the lure is basically the thing that you're giving people to entice them to become a lead. And I'm going to show you how actually you don't need to give them anything extra. This is about starting them on the sales journey and getting them to move through your sales process um actually faster than they would be otherwise. It's a key topic for service businesses. We're then going to look at objection handling and how to handle objections on your website. So, we're all familiar with objection handling during the sales process. And we know that um for example, when you tell someone the price of something and they say, "Oh, that sounds a bit expensive." Then you might have rehearsed a way to kind of come up with uh you know, an answer which overcomes that objection. But what we don't do is think about objections on our websites. Now, the objections that people come up with when they're browsing your website aren't necessarily to against buying from you. They might be against getting in contact with you. They might be if you're selling a product through an e-commerce store, they might be about buying from you. But quite often the objection is actually caused by uncertainty and fear rather than a clear, you know, a financial objection or uh a typical objection that you might get during the sales process. In the video after that, we're going to look at how to demonstrate social proof. The key with social proof is we never want a website visitor to feel like they are the first person making that decision to buy from you. We want them to land on your website and think lots of people have been in the situation I'm now in. Lots of people have made this same decision which I'm contemplating and they're happy with that decision. That's the process that we want people to go through and this can happen instantaneously. It doesn't have to be, you know, conscious like I've just described. This is some this is a decision that we're making very, very quickly. We're then going to look at ease and how we can make what I call a slippery slide process for your website visitors. Now, if you imagine most websites, if you want to become a lead or sale, firstly, you've got to hunt around to find the thing that you need to do. Then you've got to take a big risk. Uh you don't know exactly what's going to happen when you get in contact with them. And then they might have unnecessary form fields. They might basically they put blockages in the way from you. We call them conversion blockers. And ease of use is all about removing as many of these conversion blockers as possible so that when someone lands on your website, they're kind of sliding down this slippery slide into becoming a customer with you. And then finally, we're going to look at how to deliver a result through your conversion process. So, how to actually make this is all
